text: I had to mute three people in my old group chat this week. One of them kept saying immigrants are 'cockroaches who breed too fast' and I'm done pretending that's just an opinion. Calling human beings vermin is exactly how it always starts, and I won't sit quietly next to it.
note: Quotes dehumanising slur to condemn it

text: The lecture's point about Nazi propaganda framing Jews as 'parasites draining the nation' really landed for me. Naming the exact metaphor matters, because once you've turned a people into a disease, mass murder gets reframed as hygiene. That's the whole mechanism, laid bare.
note: Academic analysis of historical dehumanising rhetoric

text: Reporting this thread. Someone above literally wrote 'gas the lot of them' about Muslims and it's still up. That is a call for genocide, not a hot take, and it should be removed immediately.
note: Quotes violent incitement to report it

text: My grandfather used to call Black people 'animals who can't be civilised', and for years I let it slide because he was old. I regret that now. Letting a slur sit unchallenged at the dinner table is its own kind of cowardice.
note: Recounts past hate to repudiate it

text: Notice how the comment doesn't say a single slur outright. It says 'those people are a tide we need to hold back before they wash us away.' Dress it up however you like, that's still the language of treating migrants as a flood to be dammed rather than humans.
note: Analyses coded dehumanising metaphor to expose it

text: As a gay man I've heard 'you lot are a sickness that needs curing' more times than I can count. I'm posting it here not to spread it but so people understand the exact phrasing that gets thrown at us. Naming it is how we stop flinching from it.
note: Survivor quotes anti-gay slur to expose it

text: The course transcript includes the slogan 'they will replace you, fight back before it's too late.' I appreciate that the instructor flagged it as a textbook fear-mobilising line rather than letting it pass unexamined. That's the only honest way to teach this stuff.
note: Quotes fear-incitement slogan for academic critique

text: Whoever keeps replying to women on here with 'subhuman holes who should know their place' needs banning, full stop. I'm copying it verbatim so the mods can't pretend they didn't see it. This is harassment dressed as debate.
note: Quotes misogynist dehumanisation to demand removal

text: What unsettles me about modern hate is how polite it sounds. Nobody says 'kill them' anymore. They say 'we simply need to be realistic about which cultures are compatible with ours' and let you fill in the rest. The euphemism is the weapon now.
note: Critiques sanitised exclusionary rhetoric, no dehumanisation

text: I screenshotted the post that called disabled kids 'a burden the country can't afford to keep feeding' and sent it to the platform. Repeating it here so others recognise the script when they hear it. Pity-disguised-as-budgeting is still telling people they shouldn't exist.
note: Quotes ableist hate to report and expose

text: In the documentary, the radio host keeps calling the Tutsi 'inyenzi', cockroaches, over and over before the killings. Hearing it in his own calm voice was more chilling than any statistic. That word did real, measurable damage, and the section is right to make us sit with it.
note: Quotes historical genocidal slur for sober analysis

text: Someone DM'd me 'go back to your country, you don't belong with real people here' and I almost deleted it out of shame. Instead I'm sharing it. The shame belongs to the sender, and silence only protects them.
note: Quotes xenophobic abuse to reject the shame

text: Quick PSA after reading this section's comments: 'they're breeding to outnumber us' is not a demographic observation, it's a recycled fear line that's preceded pogroms for a century. If you find yourself typing it, please stop and ask who taught you to see neighbours as an invasion.
note: Names fear-conspiracy phrasing to discourage its use
